findings.title: Staged tarball assertion is not install-specific
findings.why_it_matters: An unrelated or incorrectly located argument ending in release-candidate.tgz can satisfy this assertion, so a regression that stops passing the private staged copy to npm install could pass the release gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Isolate the npm log line appended by the candidate update, assert that it is the install invocation, and assert that its tarball argument starts under $TMPDIR/mcp-bpmn-install. and ends in /release-candidate.tgz.
evidence: The changed assertion searches the entire cumulative npm log for only '/release-candidate.tgz>', without checking the command or staging-directory prefix.
The fake npm records every invocation in the same npm.log (tests/install-agent-integrations.test.sh:84-92), so the match is not tied to the candidate update's npm install call.

The installer creates the private staging directory with mktemp and passes $TEMP_DIR/release-candidate.tgz to npm install (scripts/install-agent-integrations.sh:802-839, 863-867), which is the behavior the acceptance criterion requires the test to pin.

residual_risks: The 40-second Jest deadline covers the entire long structured-output test while its SVG call alone may consume 25 seconds; serialization removes the observed contention, but hosted-runner headroom for the surrounding calls and cleanup is not established by the diff itself.
